column7: MigrateUserToMachine created the machine identity in its own transaction and then suspended the source user in a second one, so any refusal or failure in the suspension left a new machine identity beside a still-ACTIVE human account with live sessions and PATs -- reported to the caller as a partial state for an operator to finish by hand. Reachable on ORDINARY input, not only under injected faults: the admin-rank ceiling (an actor who does not outrank the target) and guardLastAdminDeactivation (a last-admin target) were both evaluated AFTER the identity had committed. Fixed by hoisting both refusals and the input validation ahead of any write and committing the identity insert and the suspension in ONE WithTransaction inside the existing named lock, with cache eviction and all three audit events after commit; setAccountState was split into setAccountStateInTx (its transaction body, returning the hashes to evict) so the two writes can share a transaction without changing single-write behaviour. Three sibling tests cover the other angles: _UnderRankedActorCreatesNoIdentity and _LastAdminTargetCreatesNoIdentity (refused, zero identities, target unchanged) and _HappyPathCommitsBothAndAudits (so the three negative assertions cannot be satisfied by a function that never works). All four run against a real SQLite transaction, since a mock WithTransaction runs its closure inline and cannot demonstrate a rollback. Found by FIX-2 review on PR #2812; root-caused as an atomicity-guard detector gap (atomicityWriteVerbRe had no Suspend, so only one of the two writes was counted and the function never reached the 2-write threshold), fixed as a product change on coordinator decision rather than classified as an exemption.
